content: The combination of elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF interacts with various drugs by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism, particularly through CYP3A4, CYP2C9, and CYP2D6 pathways. These interactions can lead to increased or decreased drug levels, necessitating careful monitoring and potential therapy adjustments. Below are the detailed interactions: 1. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and levoketoconazole: Both drugs inhibit CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing each other's levels. Do not exceed a ketoconazole dose of 200 mg/day. Monitor therapy closely. 2. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and levomilnacipran: This combination increases levomilnacipran levels. Limit levomilnacipran to 80 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor therapy closely. 3. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and lidocaine: Lidocaine levels may increase due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor therapy closely. 4. Cobicistat and CYP3A4 substrates: Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates where elevated plasma concentrations may cause serious or life-threatening events. 5. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and losartan: This combination increases losartan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition but decreases levels via CYP2C9 induction. Use caution and monitor therapy. 6. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and lumacaftor/ivacaftor: No dose adjustment is needed unless initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor with strong CYP3A inhibitors, in which case reduce the dose initially. 7. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and lumateperone: Lumateperone levels increase with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Limit lumateperone to 5 mg/day. Monitor therapy closely. 8. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and magnesium oxide: Magnesium oxide reduces elvitegravir absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. Monitor therapy. 9. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and maprotiline: Maprotiline levels increase due to CYP2D6 inhibition. Monitor therapy closely. 10. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and methotrexate or methoxyflurane: Both combinations increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and methylprednisolone: Methylprednisolone levels increase due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor therapy closely. 12. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and methamphetamine: Methamphetamine levels increase due to CYP2D6 inhibition. Monitor therapy closely. 13. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and modafinil: Modafinil levels increase due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor therapy closely. 14. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and mometasone (inhaled or intranasal): Mometasone levels increase, raising the risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects. Use caution and monitor therapy. 15. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and montelukast: Montelukast levels increase via CYP3A4 inhibition but decrease via CYP2C9 induction. Use caution and monitor therapy. 16. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and NSAIDs (e.g., meloxicam, naproxen, piroxicam): Co-administration may increase toxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs and monitor therapy closely. 17. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and norgestimate/norgestrel: Norgestimate levels increase, potentially causing insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, acne, and venous thrombosis. Ethinyl estradiol levels may decrease, reducing contraceptive efficacy. Monitor therapy closely. 18. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and ondansetron: Ondansetron levels increase due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor therapy closely. 19. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and oxaliplatin: Increased nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity may occur. Use caution and monitor therapy. 20. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and oxycodone: Oxycodone levels increase due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor therapy closely. 21. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and paricalcitol: Paricalcitol levels increase due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor therapy closely. 22. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and pazopanib: Pazopanib levels increase due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor therapy closely. 23. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and phenytoin: Phenytoin levels decrease due to CYP2C9 induction. Use caution and monitor therapy. 24. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and quazepam: Quazepam levels increase due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider reducing the benzodiazepine dose. Monitor therapy closely. 25. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and quinidine: Quinidine levels increase due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor therapy closely. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when co-administering elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF with other medications, particularly those metabolized by CYP enzymes.
